api: No official public API. Automation depends on unofficial routes, which carry their own terms-of-service risk.
cons: No commercial indemnity comparable to Adobe's
name: Midjourney
pros: Best output aesthetics in the category
files: Text prompts plus image references for style and composition control.
value: Consistently the strongest output aesthetics in the category. Chosen where the image has to look genuinely good rather than merely correct.
engine: Proprietary image models. Not open weight.
latency: Seconds per generation, typically several variants at once.

pricing.includes: More fast time, relaxed unlimited generation
Highest quotas, stealth mode on upper tiers

quality: Best-in-class aesthetics. Weaker than peers at rendering legible text in images and at precise, literal instruction-following.
tagline: The aesthetic leader in image generation, with the least clear commercial-use position.
use_cases: Concept art, mood boards, and campaign visual exploration
Marketing imagery where style consistency matters
Rapid visual iteration before commissioning real production
governance_note: Two live issues. First, the public-by-default behaviour: staff experimenting with an unreleased product name or design are publishing it. Second, the training-data provenance question that image generators face collectively, which is the subject of ongoing litigation and which Midjourney has not resolved through licensing the way Adobe has. Where indemnity matters more than aesthetics, Firefly is the safer choice, and the reference library's copyright material is the place to start.
training_optout: Generations are public by default on lower tiers. Private generation requires an upper tier. That default alone disqualifies it for confidential product work unless the tier is chosen deliberately.
